cards.headline: Linkages reveal financial statement interdependencies
cards.one_thing: Link income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements to trace financial flows.
cards.narration: This session builds on yesterday’s introduction to linkages by using Mash Direct Ltd’s FY2025 accounts and *Financial Intelligence* chapter 3. Focus is on how income statement profits affect retained earnings (balance sheet) and cash flow from operations. The book explains how accruals and cash flows differ, while the accounts show real-world examples of these relationships.

ideas.label: Statement connections
ideas.text: Income statement profits increase retained earnings on the balance sheet.

ideas.label: Cash flow linkages
ideas.text: Operating cash flow adjusts net income for non-cash items like depreciation.

ideas.label: Accruals impact
ideas.text: Accruals affect income statement timing but not immediate cash flow.

example.title: Mash Direct Ltd FY2025 illustrative example
example.takeaway: Profit influences balance sheet and cash flow, but not directly.

flow.note: Identify profit figures.
Locate retained earnings changes.
Note adjustments to net income.
Spot non-cash items in cash flow.
Align with book’s linkage examples.

cards.do_today: Analyze Mash Direct Ltd’s FY2025 accounts and *Financial Intelligence* chapter 3 to map financial statement connections. Produce a 1-page summary.
cards.handoff: Tomorrow’s session will explore how accruals affect revenue recognition and financial statements.
cards.summary: Linkages show how financial statements interconnect, guiding tomorrow’s accruals discussion.

cards.headline: Accruals track income and expenses when they occur, not when paid
cards.one_thing: Accrual accounting matches revenues and expenses to the period they're incurred, not cash flow timing
cards.narration: Yesterday’s linkage discussion showed how financial statements connect. Today, we apply this to accruals: income and expenses are recorded when earned/incurred, not when cash changes hands. Chapter 5 of *Financial Intelligence* explains this, focusing on revenue recognition rules. This method ensures financial statements reflect true business performance across periods, even if cash flows differ.

ideas.label: Matching principle
ideas.text: Revenues and expenses are paired to the period they relate to, not cash timing

ideas.label: Revenue timing
ideas.text: Revenue is recorded when earned, not when cash is received

ideas.label: Statement impact
ideas.text: Accruals affect balance sheets (liabilities/assets) and income statements

example.title: Illustrative accrual
example.takeaway: Revenue is recognized when earned, not when cash is received

flow.note: Determine if revenue/expense has occurred
Assign to correct accounting period
Update income and balance sheets

cards.do_today: Read *Financial Intelligence* chapter 5. Define accrual principles and note revenue recognition rules. Produce a summary document
cards.handoff: Tomorrow’s revenue standards will detail specific rules for when revenue is recognized under IFRS
cards.summary: Accruals ensure financial statements reflect true performance by matching revenues and expenses to the correct period, preparing for tomorrow’s revenue standards discussion

cards.headline: IFRS 15 and GAAP differ in revenue recognition timing
cards.one_thing: IFRS 15 uses a five-step model; GAAP focuses on core revenue principle with fewer steps.
cards.narration: Yesterday’s accruals discussion prepares for today’s revenue standards. Around Noon Ltd’s FY2024 accounts will highlight differences between IFRS 15 and GAAP. Both standards aim to match revenues with expenses but use distinct criteria for when revenue is recognised. This affects financial statements’ timing and presentation.

ideas.label: IFRS 15
ideas.text: Requires identifying performance obligations and allocating transaction price.

ideas.label: GAAP
ideas.text: Emphasises contract modifications and five criteria for revenue recognition.

ideas.label: Impact
ideas.text: Differences may delay or accelerate revenue recognition in financial statements.

example.title: Revenue recognition comparison
example.takeaway: Timing differences arise from distinct criteria in IFRS 15 and GAAP.

flow.note: Link to yesterday’s session on matching revenues and expenses.
Identify key differences in revenue recognition criteria.
Use Around Noon Ltd’s FY2024 data for practical application.
Note where IFRS 15 and GAAP produce different outcomes.
Prepare summary for tomorrow’s linkage discussion.

cards.do_today: Compare IFRS 15 and GAAP revenue recognition using Around Noon Ltd’s FY2024 accounts; produce a summary table highlighting differences.
cards.handoff: Tomorrow’s session will apply these differences to link revenue recognition with broader financial reporting.
cards.summary: IFRS 15 and GAAP use different approaches to timing revenue recognition, affecting financial statements’ presentation.

cards.headline: Cash flow impacts shape P&L and balance sheet linkages
cards.one_thing: Different revenue recognition rules under IFRS 15 and GAAP alter financial statement timing and presentation.
cards.narration: Yesterday’s session showed how revenue timing differs between IFRS 15 and GAAP. Today, apply this to trace cash flow effects on income statements and balance sheets using lab companies like Hannan Meats Ltd or alternatives if P&L data is missing.

ideas.label: Linkage
ideas.text: Cash flow from operations directly affects retained earnings on the balance sheet and revenue on the P&L.

ideas.label: Exemption
ideas.text: Hannan Meats Ltd uses small-company regime filings; check for P&L inclusion before proceeding.

ideas.label: Alternative
ideas.text: If Hannan Meats lacks P&L data, use Mash Direct Ltd (FY2025) or Around Noon Ltd (FY2024) with full accounts.

example.title: Illustrative cash flow impact
example.takeaway: Cash flow directly increases both P&L revenue and retained earnings.

flow.note: Use Hannan Meats if P&L is available.
Extract operating cash flow figures from accounts.
Map cash flow to revenue recognition timing.
Update retained earnings based on P&L changes.
Record linkages in analysis file.

cards.do_today: Trace cash flow impacts on P&L and balance sheet for chosen company; produce analysis file with findings.
cards.handoff: Tomorrow’s session will build on this by creating a linkage analysis model.
cards.summary: Today’s task focused on applying cash flow linkages to P&L and balance sheets using lab company data.

cards.headline: Mash Direct Ltd FY2025: Link Income Statement to Cash Flow
cards.one_thing: Changes in working capital (e.g., receivables, payables) directly impact cash flow from operations, not just profit.
cards.narration: Yesterday’s session used lab company data to apply cash flow linkages to P&L and balance sheets. Today’s task focuses on Mash Direct Ltd’s FY2025 accounts. Produce a 2-page report reconciling net income with cash flow from operations, checking how accruals and working capital adjustments affect cash flow.

ideas.label: Working capital adjustments
ideas.text: Changes in receivables/payables alter cash flow from operations, independent of profit.

ideas.label: Non-cash items
ideas.text: Depreciation and amortisation are added back to net income in cash flow calculations.

ideas.label: Accruals impact
ideas.text: Accruals (e.g., accrued expenses) affect both P&L and cash flow timing differences.

example.title: Illustrative reconciliation
example.takeaway: Adjust net income by adding back non-cash items and working capital changes to arrive at cash flow from operations.

flow.note: Take FY2025 income statement figure.
Include depreciation, amortisation.
Compare FY2024 and FY2025 receivables/payables.
Ensure alignment with operating activities section.
Identify timing differences in revenue/expenses.

cards.do_today: Build a 2-page report analysing Mash Direct Ltd’s FY2025 linkages between income statement and cash flow statement. Output: file.
cards.handoff: Tomorrow’s build 2 will audit accruals, so highlight any discrepancies in timing differences for tomorrow’s analysis.
cards.summary: Today’s report links income statement figures to cash flow, focusing on working capital and accruals adjustments, preparing for tomorrow’s accruals audit.

cards.headline: Around Noon Ltd's revenue recognition and accruals adjustments require scrutiny
cards.one_thing: Accruals adjust revenue timing; verify alignment with IFRS 15 and working capital flows
cards.narration: Yesterday linked income statement figures to cash flow, highlighting working capital impacts. Today’s task focuses on Around Noon Ltd’s FY2024 revenue recognition practices and accrual adjustments, ensuring compliance with IFRS 15 and accurate financial reporting. Using the company’s full accounts, the analysis will examine when revenue is recorded versus cash received, identify accruals adjustments for unbilled revenue or accrued expenses, and assess their impact on working capital. This builds on yesterday’s focus on cash flow linkages, moving toward tomorrow’s week review.

ideas.label: Revenue Timing
ideas.text: Revenue recognition under IFRS 15 depends on control transfer, not cash receipt.

ideas.label: Accrual Adjustments
ideas.text: Accruals adjust income statement figures to reflect economic reality, not just cash flows.

ideas.label: Working Capital
ideas.text: Accruals affect working capital by delaying or accelerating cash flows relative to revenue.

example.title: Illustrative accruals adjustment
example.takeaway: Accruals reduce net revenue by adjusting timing discrepancies between revenue recognition and cash flow.

flow.note: Identify revenue figures and accruals line items
Check unbilled revenue and accrued expenses
Link accruals to working capital changes
Verify revenue recognition timing against control transfer
Structure findings by revenue practices, accruals, and compliance

cards.do_today: Create a 3-page analysis of Around Noon Ltd FY2024 revenue recognition practices and accrual adjustments, producing a file for review
cards.handoff: Tomorrow’s week review will assess how today’s accruals audit informs understanding of financial statement accuracy.
cards.summary: Today’s analysis of Around Noon Ltd’s revenue recognition and accruals prepares for tomorrow’s week review by clarifying accruals’ impact on financial statements.

cards.headline: Accruals shape financial statements and tax outcomes
cards.one_thing: Accruals adjust revenue timing, affecting both current and future tax liabilities
cards.narration: Yesterday’s analysis of Around Noon Ltd’s revenue recognition and accruals clarifies how these adjustments influence financial statements. Today’s review links this to Financial Intelligence concepts, preparing for tomorrow’s focus on tax implications. Understanding accruals’ role in matching revenues with expenses ensures accurate financial reporting and informs tax planning strategies for the coming week.

ideas.label: Accruals Timing
ideas.text: Accruals record revenues when earned, not when cash is received, aligning financial statements with economic reality.

ideas.label: Revenue Recognition
ideas.text: Revenue is recognised when performance obligations are met, impacting both profit calculations and tax liabilities.

ideas.label: Tax Implications
ideas.text: Accrual adjustments may defer tax payments, creating short-term cash flow benefits but requiring future liability management.

example.title: Illustrative Accrual Impact
example.takeaway: This example shows how accruals reduce reported income, potentially lowering current tax but requiring future adjustments.

flow.note: Analyse Around Noon Ltd’s FY2024 figures for revenue timing.
Align findings with concepts from the book’s Chapter 6 on accrual accounting.
Estimate how accrual adjustments affect next week’s tax planning scenarios.

cards.do_today: Reconcile weekly learnings on accruals and revenue recognition, producing a 1-page summary linking concepts to practical examples
cards.handoff: Tomorrow’s session will explore how accrual adjustments influence tax liability calculations and cash flow projections.
cards.summary: Understanding accruals’ role in financial reporting ensures accurate tax planning and informed business decisions.

outline.title: Colour Palettes

outline.why: Trains palette types and semantic colour use.

outline.title: Accessible Contrast
outline.prompt: Find a visual with high text contrast; check if it meets WCAG 4.5:1.
outline.why: Practices colour-blind-safe palettes and contrast standards.

outline.title: Type Scales

outline.why: Reinforces line length and weight-before-size principles.

outline.title: Grid Layouts

outline.title: Semantic Accent

outline.why: Strengthens use of accent colour for 'look here' cues.

outline.why: Consolidates colour, type, and grid understanding.

sunday.headline: Build a one-page HTML test with defined type scale and 5-colour palette
sunday.one_thing: Use HSL, type scales, and grids to replace default choices with deliberate design decisions
sunday.narration: Yesterday’s focus on colour, type, and grids leads to today’s build. Apply HSL palettes, modular type scales, and column grids to create a one-page HTML artifact. Check contrast ratios and refine layouts using the spine’s critique stage. Deliverables include the test page, colour/type notes, and completed critiques.

ideas.label: HSL thinking
ideas.text: Use HSL to define 5-colour palettes with one semantic accent and greys as base.

ideas.label: Modular type scale
ideas.text: Set a base font size (e.g., 16px) and calculate increments (e.g., 1.25x) for consistent hierarchy.

ideas.label: Column grids
ideas.text: Use 4/8px spacing scales and bento layouts to align content with F/Z reading patterns.

example.title: Sample type scale and palette
example.takeaway: Use this structure to ensure readability and accessibility in the HTML test.

flow.note: Set audience, takeaway, and format constraints for the test page.
Select 5 HSL colours with WCAG AA contrast (4.5:1) for text and background.
Apply type scale and column grids using a 4/8px spacing scale.
Use a contrast checker to validate text and background colour pairs.
Adjust alignment and spacing to follow F/Z reading patterns.

sunday.do_today: Build a one-page HTML artifact with Claude using a stated type scale and 5-colour palette; check contrast with a checker. Deliver: colour/type/grid note, 7 critiques, one-page test.
sunday.handoff: Tomorrow’s focus shifts to refining the test page using feedback from today’s critiques.
sunday.summary: Today’s session applied colour, type, and grid principles to build a test page, checked contrast, and completed critiques.
